seoTitle: How to Create a Knowledge Base in Zendesk Easily (2026)
metaDescription: Build a Zendesk knowledge base: confirm your plan includes it, create a category and sections, then write and publish your first article with the right visibility.
intro: Every support team eventually hits the same wall: the same few questions keep landing in the ticket queue, and answering them one by one doesn't scale. Zendesk's Knowledge base (Guide) turns those repeat answers into a searchable Help Center article customers can find themselves. This guide follows the actual setup path, from the plan requirement people miss, through categories and sections, to writing an article with the right visibility, so the structure holds up as more content gets added later.
prerequisites: Admin or Knowledge-admin access in Zendesk, since only those roles can create categories and sections
costNote: Help Center (Guide) isn't included in Zendesk's standalone Support plans. It's bundled starting with the Suite Team plan and up, so if Knowledge admin doesn't appear in your Admin Center, check whether your account is on a Support-only plan rather than assuming it's a permissions issue.

steps.heading: Confirm your plan includes Guide, then open Knowledge admin
steps.body: Help Center is a Suite-plan feature, not something every Zendesk account has by default. If you're on a Support-only plan, Knowledge admin won't appear in Admin Center at all, no matter what permissions your account has. Once that's confirmed, Admin Center is where the rest of this setup happens.

image.caption: The Admin Center home screen, the starting point for reaching Knowledge admin and confirming Help Center is available on this plan.

steps.heading: Create your first category
steps.body: Inside Knowledge admin, click Add and choose Category. The form is short: a Name field, an optional Description, and a Source language selector so you know which language variant you're editing if your Help Center supports more than one. Categories are the top level of your knowledge base's structure, the main folders customers browse first, like "Product Information," "Billing," or "Getting Started." Name them around how customers think about your product, not your internal team structure. One quirk worth knowing: if your Help Center only ever has a single category, it stays hidden from customers, who see just the sections inside it.

image.caption: The Add category form, with a category named "Product Information" ready to hold the sections and articles underneath it.

steps.heading: Add sections inside the category
steps.body: Articles can't sit directly inside a category in Zendesk; they need a section first. Click Add and choose Section, give it a name and optional description, and under Hierarchy pick which category (or section) it nests under. A "Product Information" category might break down into sections like "Setup," "Troubleshooting," and "FAQs." Sections can nest inside other sections too, up to five levels deep with as many as 200 sections under one section, but most support content only needs two levels, category then section. Going deeper tends to bury articles instead of organizing them.

steps.heading: Write your first article and set who can see it
steps.body: From Knowledge admin, start a new article and place it inside a section. The editor opens with a title field, start with something specific like "How to reset your password" rather than a vague label, and a formatting toolbar for headings, links, images, tables, and embeds. On the right, Article settings controls who can edit it (Management permissions, defaulting to Administrators), where it's placed, who's listed as the author, and critically, Visible to. That last setting defaults to Agents and admins, which keeps a new article internal-only. If the goal is a self-service article customers can find on their own, change Visible to your public or signed-in-customer segment before publishing, otherwise the article exists but nobody outside the team can see it.

image.caption: The article editor with a title in progress and the Article settings panel on the right, covering permissions, placement, author, and the Visible to setting.

steps.heading: Publish and test the search
steps.body: Once the content, placement, and visibility all look right, save and publish. Then test it the way a real customer would: search the Help Center for the phrase you'd expect them to type, not the internal title given to the article. If it doesn't surface easily, add a few more content tags or adjust the title's wording. An article that's accurate but unfindable doesn't save anyone support time.

faq.question: Does every Zendesk plan include a knowledge base?
faq.answer: No. Help Center (Guide) is bundled with Zendesk's Suite plans starting at Suite Team; it isn't part of the standalone Support plans. If Knowledge admin isn't showing up, check the plan before troubleshooting permissions.

faq.question: What's the difference between a category and a section in Zendesk Guide?
faq.answer: A category is the top-level grouping customers browse first, like "Product Information" or "Billing." Sections sit underneath a category, or another section, and break it down further, like "Setup" or "Troubleshooting." Articles live inside sections, never directly inside a category.

faq.question: Why can't customers see my new knowledge base article?
faq.answer: Check the Visible to setting in Article settings. New articles default to Agents and admins only, so they stay internal until you widen visibility to your public or customer segment.

faq.question: How deep can I nest categories and sections?
faq.answer: Sections can nest inside other sections up to five levels deep, with up to 200 sections under any one section. Most support content only needs two levels: a category, then a section.

faq.question: How do I know if my knowledge base articles are actually findable?
faq.answer: Search the Help Center using the phrases a customer would realistically type, not the internal article title. If it doesn't surface easily, adjust the title or add more content tags.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a Knowledge admin walkthrough. The category/section hierarchy rules and the article-placement constraint were re-checked against Zendesk's official support documentation in September 2026, and the plan requirement was checked against Zendesk's official pricing page. This corrected two things this guide previously implied: that a category alone could hold an article (it can't, a section is required), and that Guide is available on every plan (it's a Suite-plan feature).
